title: Of Dreams & Shadows - is there room in your collection for mid-tier games?
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hBqhV23fZnE

Having pulled Of Dreams & Shadows off the shelf to show the box during his Lost Ones episode, Daniel (@dungeondive) decided to relearn it and play — and uses it to ask a question worth asking of any curated collection: is there room for mid-tier games, or should you only keep the best?

He is clear about the tier. Overland adventure games are his favourite genre, and against Talisman, Runebound, Arkham Horror and Eldritch Horror this one is solidly C. The art is the exception — Matt Forsyth and Simon Buckroy's illustrations are gorgeous — but the map is dull, all flat white lines and basic iconography, which he can't account for given everything around it.

What keeps it on the shelf is that it does enough right. Heroes test a D6 against an attribute, willpower doubles as a currency for buying off bad luck, and the whole thing is a threat-management race across two acts before the boss arrives. The quest writing is good. One run produced a plague-town encounter that spawned an undead horde a single space from a capital, perfectly matching the undead boss he was fighting. The expansion, he says flatly, you can skip.

----

Does your collection have space for a once-a-year C-tier game, or does every box have to earn its shelf?
